Counts what you don\'t.
Reelometer counts the short videos you watch on TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts: how many, how long, on which topics and from which creators. The data is yours; the conclusions are too.
%1$s OF SCREEN TIME
A counter going up to %1$s.
What you watch stays here.
NO ACCOUNTS
No sign-up, no email, no password.
NO SERVERS
Everything is stored on this phone. There is no copy anywhere else.
NO ADS
No ads and no trackers. Nobody else looks at your data.
NO INTERNET
The app has no permission to connect. Even if it wanted to, it couldn\'t send anything.
ON THIS PHONE ONLY
If you uninstall the app, everything goes with it.
A switch and an “Allow”.
Tap OPEN ACCESSIBILITY: I\'ll take you to Android\'s settings.
Look for “Reelometer” under “Downloaded apps”. On some phones it is under “Installed apps” or “Installed services”.
Tap “Reelometer” and turn on “Use Reelometer”.

Android will ask “Allow Reelometer to have full control of your device?”. It is the standard prompt for any accessibility service: Reelometer looks and counts, and only taps for you if you use quick send on Instagram or TikTok. Tap “Allow”.
Come back here. If the counter says OK, you\'re done.
WAITING FOR THE SERVICE
OK

SEEING “RESTRICTED SETTING”?
Is Android saying “Restricted setting”?
It\'s an Android protection for apps installed from outside Google Play, not a bug. Here is how to lift it:
Tap OPEN APP INFO.
In “App info”, tap the ⋮ menu at the top right.
Tap “Allow restricted settings” and confirm with your PIN, pattern or fingerprint.
Go back to Accessibility and turn on “Use Reelometer”.
“Allow restricted settings” only appears after Android has blocked you once. If you can\'t see it, try turning the service on first and then come back here.

ON, NOT CONNECTED
It’s on, but Android hasn’t started it

The Accessibility switch is on, but the system hasn’t started the service, so I’m not counting anything. It happens mostly on Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO, and on other phones that close apps to save battery. Here’s the fix:

Steps for your phone
Tap OPEN AUTOSTART and turn on Reelometer. On HyperOS it’s also in Settings › Apps › Permissions › “Autostart”.
Tap OPEN BATTERY SAVER and choose “No restrictions”.
In recent apps, long-press the Reelometer card and tap the padlock.
Tap OPEN APP INFO, go to “Battery” and choose “Unrestricted”.
Tap OPEN BATTERY, go to “Background usage limits” › “Never sleeping apps” and add Reelometer.
In Recents, tap the Reelometer icon and choose “Keep open”.
Tap OPEN APP LAUNCH, find Reelometer, turn off “Manage automatically” and leave all three switches on.
In recent apps, swipe the Reelometer card down to lock it.
Tap OPEN AUTOSTART and turn on Reelometer.
Tap OPEN APP INFO, go to “Battery usage” and turn on “Allow background activity”.
In Recents, open the menu on the Reelometer card and choose “Lock”.
Tap OPEN BATTERY, go to “High background power consumption” and allow Reelometer.
If your phone has “Autostart” or “Protected apps”, turn on Reelometer there too.

Tap OPEN APP INFO and turn off “Pause app activity if unused” (on older phones, “Remove permissions if app isn’t used”). Reelometer works without you opening it, so Android may take it for an unused app.
Tap OPEN ACCESSIBILITY, turn “Use Reelometer” off and then on again.

Your phone closed Reelometer when you cleared your recent apps. Lock it in recents and turn the service off and on again in Accessibility.
Your phone closed Reelometer because it was low on memory. Remove its battery restrictions and turn the service off and on again in Accessibility.
Your phone closed Reelometer on its own. Allow autostart, remove its battery restrictions and turn the service off and on again in Accessibility.
Your phone’s battery saver froze or closed Reelometer. Remove its battery restrictions and turn the service off and on again in Accessibility.
Reelometer was force stopped or its data was cleared. Turn the service off and on again in Accessibility so it counts again.
Reelometer closed because of a bug in the app itself, not because of your phone. Turn the service off and on again in Accessibility. If it happens again, share the Calibration log.
Your phone turned the service off

You didn’t turn it off: your phone closed Reelometer on its own and, in doing so, removed the service from Accessibility. Nothing you’ve watched since then has been counted. Turn it back on with these steps and then I’ll show you how to stop it happening again.
